focus: rust-anything's own Rust style — manifest, layout, errors, CLI, serde, tests, finish gate
noveltyJustification: All 11 findings are new to the packet: iteration 1 has no prior state, and each finding pairs a rust-anything file:line with a sk-code file:line coverage verdict.
keyQuestions: How is rust-anything's own Rust written: Cargo.toml lints, edition and rust-version, module layout across src/, error handling, the clap CLI, serde settings, test layout and fixtures under tests/, and the cargo fmt, clippy and test finish gate in its CLAUDE.md?
ruledOut: Reading the manifest as a workspace root
Treating anyhow in src/ as a violation to report

label: rust-anything is a single package, not a workspace, on edition 2024 with rust-version 1.97; sk-code's toolchain rule is written only in workspace terms and has no single-crate branch

Lint policy is unsafe_code=forbid plus clippy all at warn with priority -1 and deliberately no pedantic; sk-code prescribes deny plus pedantic, so it contradicts on both counts and lacks the priority idiom

serde_json is configured with float_roundtrip, preserve_order and unbounded_depth with the reason in the manifest; sk-code mentions none of them, and float_roundtrip is the rule any JSON port needs to compare floats
The CLI is clap 4 derive: a Parser struct holding one Subcommand enum, help text in doc comments, per-field arg attributes; clap appears zero times in the sk-code Rust references and checklist
Exit contract is fn main() -> ExitCode with run() -> Result<ExitCode>, error: {e:#} on stderr and exit 2 for any error; ExitCode appears zero times in the sk-code Rust set
Broken-pipe safety comes from say!/say_raw! macros that discard the write result so prog | head does not panic; no sk-code file mentions broken pipe, SIGPIPE or stdout().lock()
Error handling splits by layer: anyhow in the binary and 56 src files, thiserror in 2; sk-code covers the binary half at P2 and contradicts the library half at P0, and the set is right
Panic discipline is machine-checked with a five-token PANICS scan and an INFALLIBLE: escape marker that skips #[cfg(test)]; sk-code has no unwrap/expect/panic policy and no escape-marker convention

Finish gate is cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test plus an obligation to update docs/STATUS.md when what works changed; sk-code covers the commands more strictly but lacks the documentation clause

Module layout is a flat pub mod list in lib.rs with test-only modules gated and the MSRV single-sourced via env!(CARGO_PKG_RUST_VERSION); sk-code requires rust-version but never says to read it back from Cargo

Tests are 44 integration files under tests/ named for the failure they pin, sharing tests/common/mod.rs and a per-language tests/fixtures/ tree; sk-code mentions fixtures but not the name-for-the-failure convention

direction: Reading the manifest as a workspace root
reason: grep for [workspace] in Cargo.toml returns nothing; the package is the root, so sk-code's workspace-only rule has no branch for this shape

direction: Treating anyhow in src/ as a violation to report
reason: sk-code's P2 clause permits anyhow in an outermost non-ABI application shell, which is what rust-anything's main is; the finding was re-scoped to the library-module half
